messages:
Alice Lee: Quick question re: CMK integration for Private deployments. We need an agreed RBAC model for who can register/import keys, who can perform wrap/unwrap (data key operations), and what audit events we surface to customers. Also customers asking about retention and signed evidence. Thoughts?

Ben Ortiz: +1. My high-level suggestion: separate roles so no one person or service has both import/delete and decrypt. Proposed roles: key-admin (register/import/rotate/delete), key-operator (trigger rewraps/rotation jobs, emergency revoke), service-account (only envelope encrypt/decrypt).

Emily (sec): For SOC2/ISO reqs we need separation of duties. key-admin must NOT have Decrypt. All sensitive key ops must be logged to both provider audit (e.g., CloudTrail) and our Redwood audit store with immutable append-only entries.

Frank (infra): Implementation notes: customers can import key material into an HSM-backed KMS (BYOK). We enforce a non-exportable / no-extract flag at import time. On our side, any wrap/unwrap request goes through a short-lived service principal token and is scoped by RBAC.

Alice Lee: Can someone sketch a minimal RBAC mapping (Redwood roles -> KMS perms) + give options for audit retention (30d / 1yr / 7yr)? A lot of compliance teams ask for multi-year retention.

Ben Ortiz: Sketch below — minimal mapping and a sample KMS policy fragment. Note this is intentionally conservative.

```yaml
# Redwood RBAC -> KMS permission mapping (example)
roles:
  key-admin:
    redwood_perms: ["cmk.register","cmk.delete","cmk.rotate"]
    kms_perms: ["kms:ImportKeyMaterial","kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion"]
  key-operator:
    redwood_perms: ["cmk.rewrap","cmk.rotate"]
    kms_perms: ["kms:Encrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey","kms:ReEncrypt"]
  service-account:
    redwood_perms: ["cmk.encrypt","cmk.decrypt"]
    kms_perms: ["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt"]
```

```json
// KMS resource policy hardening (example)
{
  "Statement": [
    { "Effect": "Deny", "Principal": "*", "Action": ["kms:ExportKeyMaterial"], "Resource": "*" }
  ]
}
```

Ben Ortiz: Audit retention options: for most customers 90d default, 1y for standard, 7y for regulated. We should surface retention tiers and an export tool for long-term storage (signed bundles).

Emily (sec): For incident playbook: if a CMK is suspected compromised -> 1) mark key as disabled; 2) import/bring-up new CMK or rotate; 3) rewrap all data keys (generate new DEKs and re-encrypt blobs); 4) kick off forensic on HSM/KMS logs and share with customer; 5) notify compliance/legal. Make sure the RBAC audit shows who executed steps 1-4.

Frank (infra): Rewrap at scale is heavy. We need: a) idempotent background job with checkpoints, b) throttling to avoid saturating GPUs/storage, c) verification step to sample-check re-encrypted objects. Also consider per-tenant staging so customers can opt-in to live rewrap windows.

Carla (ops-bot): Created ticket INC-4821: "CMK: RBAC mapping + audit export design" <https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4821> :spiral_calendar:

Alice Lee: One more: customers ask for cryptographic proof of actions (signed audit exports). Options: 1) hand off raw provider audit (CloudTrail) with proof-of-origin, 2) generate signed, timestamped audit bundles from our console (we sign with infra key + include Merkle hash chain). Which do we prefer?

Emily (sec): Signed bundles are higher trust for e-discovery. We can support both. Signed bundles increase retention and key lifecycle obligations (we must protect the infra signing key, rotate it, and include that in attestation).

Ben Ortiz: I'll draft a CR (RBAC + sample KMS policies + retention tiers + export format) and push by EOD. Will include option matrix for: no-export (most secure), signed-bundle, raw-cloudtrail pointer.

Alice Lee: Thanks — please @channel when ready. Also note we need to align with Product on UX for retention selection during Private onboarding. :eyes:

Emily (sec): Agreed. I'll add compliance checklist items for SOC2 and ISO 27001 and link in the ticket. :thumbsup:
